card.name: Linking words before outcome or amount
card.fires_on: Small linking words or verbs (to, of, until, causes, by, that) that sit right before a result, a quantity, or a level, mostly in dosing and overdose text. Words after it often describe whether an amount is enough or lacking.

modes.label: Link before result
modes.description: A small word like 'to', 'by' or 'that' leads into a consequence or cause of a dosing issue.
modes.example: it may lead<< to>> a suboptimal dosing for patients

modes.label: Verb before target level
modes.description: A verb such as 'maintain' or 'restore' comes just before the level or interval to be reached.
modes.example: Adjust the administration schedule to<< maintain>> a 3-week interval between doses.

modes.label: General web text
modes.description: A linking word before a quantity or limit in non-medical writing.
modes.example: Building a Sustainable Economy in a World<< of>> Finite Resources

card.writes: It suppresses words meaning insufficient or sufficient, so it seems to steer the next word away from adequacy terms.
card.plain: It fires on little connecting words just before a statement about an amount or outcome, and it makes 'enough/not enough' wording less likely next.
